Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Omega-3 / EPA 2–3 g/day (fish oil) [ESPEN B5-7] — lean mass + neuropathy protection; Calcium 600–1000 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) + Vitamin D 400–800 IU/day — endemic Vit D deficiency in India; Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); ELDERLY: Chair-based resistance, balance exercises (Vrikshasana/tree pose), fall prevention; supervised sessions at physiotherapy/yoga centre; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [West India (Maharashtra/Gujarat/Rajasthan)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 🔪 SURGERY [C1-1/C1-3]: ERAS protocol. Screen pre-operatively. Post-op: oral diet day 1 if tolerated. Protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day for wound healing/reconstruction. Indian foods: moong dal khichdi → dal-rice → normal diet progression. | 💉 CHEMO [C3-1/C3-2]: Maintain intake during all cycles. Common Indian patient challenge: nausea reducing dal/sabzi intake. Small frequent meals; ginger/ajwain/saunf for nausea. ONS if <75% intake. | 🐟 OMEGA-3 [B5-7]: 2–3 g EPA/day (fish oil or algae-based for vegetarians) — reduces chemo toxicity, preserves lean mass, protective against neuropathy. | ❌ [C3-3]: No glutamine. No high-dose antioxidants during chemotherapy. | 🔴 TNBC [Indian]: High incidence in young premenopausal Indian women. Aggressive chemo → highest nutritional risk. Protein priority 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day. Anti-inflammatory diet. Immunotherapy GI AE management. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Plain dry toast/khakhra (2) + adrak-tulsi tea (cold/room temp, anti-nausea); small bites; avoid strong cooking smells; saunf (fennel) water sips || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Plain khakhra/dry toast + saunf-adrak tea; coconut water sips; room-temp bland foods only; avoid sweet/fatty foods || 🍽 Lunch: Soft dal-rice (1 cup each) + 1 tsp ghee (for calories) + steamed vegetable + full-fat dahi + 1 tbsp til/sesame for calcium || 🕓 Snack: 250ml commercial ONS (Pentasure/Ensure HP) + energy-dense snack: paneer cubes (30g) / til-jaggery laddoo (1) / peanut chukli (2) || 🌙 Dinner: Moong dal khichdi (1.5 cups, soft, with ghee 1 tsp) + boiled/steamed fish / paneer curry (soft) + cooked lauki/tinda + warm haldi doodh || 🌛 Bedtime: Full-fat milk (250ml warm) + 1–2 tbsp almond/peanut butter + pinch turmeric OR 250ml ONS supplement || ✅ TASTE CHANGES: Adrak (ginger) and nimbu (lemon) enhance flavour; use hari chutney (mint-coriander); room-temp/cold foods better; metallic taste — use steel/plastic cutlery not aluminium; marinate protein in dahi+haldi. || ✅ PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (Taxane-related): Omega-3 EPA 2–3g/day protective; B12 check + supplement if deficient; B6 at RDA only (NOT high-dose); include fortified foods; walking/balance exercises. || 🧂 LIMIT (Indian context): Excess ghee/vanaspati/refined oil, maida (refined flour) products (biscuits/namkeen/puri), packaged/processed foods, high-sodium pickles/papad in excess, mithai (sweets), sugar-sweetened drinks (nimbu pani with sugar, lassi with sugar), red/processed meat. || Regional: Jowar/bajra bhakri, dal-baati (baked, not fried), matki/chana ussal; reduce sugar in sabzi/dal (Gujarati); prefer bhakhri over fried snacks. || 💰 Middle SES: Balanced home-cooking. Weekly fish/egg 2–3x. Millet rotation. Seasonal produce. Avoid processed/packaged foods marketed as 'healthy'. || 🔴 TNBC (Indian): Higher prevalence in young Indian women (<40 yrs). Highest metabolic demand. Protein 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day mandatory during chemo. Anti-inflammatory diet: haldi, adrak, omega-3, berries, green tea. Immunotherapy patients: watch for immune-related colitis — low-residue if GI symptoms. || 👴 ELDERLY INDIAN BC (≥60): Soft textures; 5–6 small meals/day; ragi-based foods for calcium; haldi doodh daily; avoid very spicy/oily foods; sarcopenia screening (grip strength); adequate protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day; Vit D 800–1000 IU/day; fall prevention exercises. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian normal) — Maintain weight. Anti-cancer diet focus.
Waist_Risk_Indian: Borderline (75–79 cm — Monitor Closely)
Bone_Density_Concern: HIGH — AI-related bone loss. DEXA annually. Calcium 600–1200 mg/day + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Anorexia/Poor Appetite; Bone Pain (Metastasis); Early Satiety; Lymphedema; Mucositis/Oral Sores; Taste Changes/Chemosensory Alteration; Vomiting; Weight Loss
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: 2–3 g EPA/DHA/day — fish oil supplement [ESPEN B5-7]
Protein_Source_Note: Vegetarian protein: dal+rice combo (complete AA), paneer, curd, soya, moong, rajma, chickpeas, tofu, amaranth
Soy_Food_Guidance: Whole soy foods (tofu/soya/edamame): 1–2 servings/day SAFE for ER+ Indian BC survivors [evidence reassuring]
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]

Post-op: oral diet day 1 if tolerated. Protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day for wound healing/reconstruction. Indian foods: moong dal khichdi → dal-rice → normal diet progression. | ☢ RADIOTHERAPY [C2-1]: Breast RT — maintain adequate protein + Vit C + Zinc for skin healing. Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600–1000 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) + Vitamin D 400–800 IU/day — endemic Vit D deficiency in India; Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Megestrol Acetate / short-term Corticosteroid — physician-prescribed [ESPEN B5-1/B5-2] (note DVT risk with megestrol in Indian patients); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; LYMPHEDEMA: Progressive resistance IS SAFE — use compression garment; start with light weights, increase gradually; BONE/JOINT PAIN: Low-impact only (swimming, yoga, walking); NO high-impact/contact; physio referral; warm mustard oil massage for joints; ELDERLY: Chair-based resistance, balance exercises (Vrikshasana/tree pose), fall prevention; supervised sessions at physiotherapy/yoga centre; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [Northeast India (Assam/Manipur/Meghalaya)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 💊 APPETITE [B5-1/B5-2]: Short-term corticosteroids or megestrol acetate (physician-prescribed). Note: megestrol — DVT risk; monitor in Indian patients with higher thrombosis predisposition. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].

Avoid very salty foods (sodium). Compression garment during exercise. Government schemes: PM Poshan, NFSA for food access. Minimise food waste. Home-cooked preferred. || ✅ UNDERWEIGHT: Fortify ALL Indian meals: add ghee/coconut oil (1 tsp extra), milk powder (2 tbsp) to dalia/oats, peanut chutney, til laddoo, dry fruits. Commercial ONS 2x/day. Target +0.5 kg/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (split: 600mg x2; food sources: ragi, dahi, sesame preferred) + Vitamin D 800–1000 IU/day (AI-related bone loss); Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; AI PATIENTS: Weight-bearing exercise ESSENTIAL for bone health (walking/stair climbing 30 min/day minimum); reduces AI-related arthralgia; ELDERLY: Chair-based resistance, balance exercises (Vrikshasana/tree pose), fall prevention; supervised sessions at physiotherapy/yoga centre; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [West India (Maharashtra/Gujarat/Rajasthan)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🥗 NUTRITION [B3-1]: Active nutritional counselling + ONS if enriched Indian diet insufficient. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No energy restriction during treatment. No unproven diets — ketogenic, prolonged fasting, 'cancer-curing' diets widely promoted on Indian social media are NOT evidence-based. | 💊 AROMATASE INHIBITOR: PRIORITY in Indian women: Vit D deficiency endemic + AI worsens bone loss → dual risk. Calcium from ragi/sesame/dairy + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise. DEXA annually. AI-arthralgia: omega-3 + haldi (turmeric) anti-inflammatory. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Plain dry toast/khakhra (2) + adrak-tulsi tea (cold/room temp, anti-nausea); small bites; avoid strong cooking smells; saunf (fennel) water sips || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Plain khakhra/dry toast + saunf-adrak tea; coconut water sips; room-temp bland foods only; avoid sweet/fatty foods || 🍽 Lunch: 2 chapati + chana masala (chickpeas — fibre + plant protein) + baingan bharta + dahi + raw salad | Legumes reduce BC recurrence || 🕓 Snack: Dhokla (2 pieces, steamed) + green coriander-mint chutney + herbal tea | Fermented: probiotic + light protein || 🌙 Dinner: 2 whole wheat chapati + moong dal (yellow, easy digest) + stir-fried palak/methi + dahi + salad | Light dinner for better sleep || 🌛 Bedtime: Chamomile or ashwagandha tea + 5 soaked almonds | Sleep quality + anti-anxiety || 🧂 LIMIT (Indian context): Excess ghee/vanaspati/refined oil, maida (refined flour) products (biscuits/namkeen/puri), packaged/processed foods, high-sodium pickles/papad in excess, mithai (sweets), sugar-sweetened drinks (nimbu pani with sugar, lassi with sugar), red/processed meat. || Regional: Jowar/bajra bhakri, dal-baati (baked, not fried), matki/chana ussal; reduce sugar in sabzi/dal (Gujarati); prefer bhakhri over fried snacks. || 💰 Middle SES: Balanced home-cooking. Weekly fish/egg 2–3x. Millet rotation. Seasonal produce. Avoid processed/packaged foods marketed as 'healthy'. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class II, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 💊 AI PATIENT — CALCIUM FOODS: Ragi (nachni) roti daily, til (sesame) chutney, rajma, dahi, paneer (in moderation), moringa leaves (sahjan), amaranth (rajgira). Sunlight exposure 15–20 min before 10am for Vit D. Annual DEXA scan. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 👴 ELDERLY INDIAN BC (≥60): Soft textures; 5–6 small meals/day; ragi-based foods for calcium; haldi doodh daily; avoid very spicy/oily foods; sarcopenia screening (grip strength); adequate protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day; Vit D 800–1000 IU/day; fall prevention exercises. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

Omega3_Recommendation: 2–3 g EPA/DHA/day — fish oil supplement [ESPEN B5-7]

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (split: 600mg x2; food sources: ragi, dahi, sesame preferred) + Vitamin D 800–1000 IU/day (AI-related bone loss); Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; LYMPHEDEMA: Progressive resistance IS SAFE — use compression garment; start with light weights, increase gradually; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); AI PATIENTS: Weight-bearing exercise ESSENTIAL for bone health (walking/stair climbing 30 min/day minimum); reduces AI-related arthralgia; ELDERLY: Chair-based resistance, balance exercises (Vrikshasana/tree pose), fall prevention; supervised sessions at physiotherapy/yoga centre; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [East India (West Bengal/Odisha/Bihar/Jharkhand)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 💊 AROMATASE INHIBITOR: PRIORITY in Indian women: Vit D deficiency endemic + AI worsens bone loss → dual risk. Calcium from ragi/sesame/dairy + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise. DEXA annually. AI-arthralgia: omega-3 + haldi (turmeric) anti-inflammatory. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Plain dry toast/khakhra (2) + adrak-tulsi tea (cold/room temp, anti-nausea); small bites; avoid strong cooking smells; saunf (fennel) water sips || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Plain khakhra/dry toast + saunf-adrak tea; coconut water sips; room-temp bland foods only; avoid sweet/fatty foods || 🍽 Lunch: Soft dal-rice (1 cup each) + 1 tsp ghee (for calories) + steamed vegetable + full-fat dahi + 1 tbsp til/sesame for calcium || 🕓 Snack: 250ml commercial ONS (Pentasure/Ensure HP) + energy-dense snack: paneer cubes (30g) / til-jaggery laddoo (1) / peanut chukli (2) || 🌙 Dinner: Moong dal khichdi (1.5 cups, soft, with ghee 1 tsp) + boiled/steamed fish / paneer curry (soft) + cooked lauki/tinda + warm haldi doodh || 🌛 Bedtime: Full-fat milk (250ml warm) + 1–2 tbsp almond/peanut butter + pinch turmeric OR 250ml ONS supplement || ✅ TASTE CHANGES: Adrak (ginger) and nimbu (lemon) enhance flavour; use hari chutney (mint-coriander); room-temp/cold foods better; metallic taste — use steel/plastic cutlery not aluminium; marinate protein in dahi+haldi. || ✅ LYMPHEDEMA: Maintain healthy weight — obesity worsens lymphedema. Adequate protein for tissue health. Avoid very salty foods (sodium). Compression garment during exercise. Progressive resistance exercise IS SAFE. || ⚖ WEIGHT NOTE (Indian BMI): Indian women are at higher metabolic risk at BMI ≥23. Obesity (BMI ≥25) significantly increases BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Post-treatment: maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 [ICMR/WHO Asian cut-offs]. || Regional: Include fish curry (omega-3) 2–3x/week for NV patients; prefer hand-pounded/red rice over polished white; dal-bhaat-sabzi as base; mustard oil (omega-3 source). || 💰 Low SES: Focus on cost-effective anti-cancer foods — seasonal vegetables, local millets, dals, eggs, sprouts. Government schemes: PM Poshan, NFSA for food access. Minimise food waste. Home-cooked preferred. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class II, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 💊 AI PATIENT — CALCIUM FOODS: Ragi (nachni) roti daily, til (sesame) chutney, rajma, dahi, paneer (in moderation), moringa leaves (sahjan), amaranth (rajgira). Sunlight exposure 15–20 min before 10am for Vit D. Annual DEXA scan. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 👴 ELDERLY INDIAN BC (≥60): Soft textures; 5–6 small meals/day; ragi-based foods for calcium; haldi doodh daily; avoid very spicy/oily foods; sarcopenia screening (grip strength); adequate protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day; Vit D 800–1000 IU/day; fall prevention exercises. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian normal) — Maintain weight. Anti-cancer diet focus.
Waist_Risk_Indian: Central Obesity (≥80 cm — Indian Women Threshold)
Hormone_Therapy: Tamoxifen → Switch to AI after 2–3 years
Bone_Density_Concern: MODERATE — Post-menopausal bone loss. DEXA screening. Calcium + Vit D + weight-bearing exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Fatigue; Peripheral Neuropathy; Taste Changes/Chemosensory Alteration; Weight Gain
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: 2–3 g EPA/DHA/day — fish oil supplement [ESPEN B5-7]
Protein_Source_Note: Vegetarian protein: dal+rice combo (complete AA), paneer, curd, soya, moong, rajma, chickpeas, tofu, amaranth
Soy_Food_Guidance: Whole soy foods (tofu/soya/edamame): 1–2 servings/day SAFE for ER+ Indian BC survivors [evidence reassuring]
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Omega-3 / EPA 2–3 g/day (algae-based DHA if vegetarian) [ESPEN B5-7] — lean mass + neuropathy protection; Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (split: 600mg x2; food sources: ragi, dahi, sesame preferred) + Vitamin D 800–1000 IU/day (AI-related bone loss); Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; AI PATIENTS: Weight-bearing exercise ESSENTIAL for bone health (walking/stair climbing 30 min/day minimum); reduces AI-related arthralgia; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [North India (UP/Delhi/Punjab/Haryana)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🥗 NUTRITION [B3-1]: Active nutritional counselling + ONS if enriched Indian diet insufficient. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No energy restriction during treatment. No unproven diets — ketogenic, prolonged fasting, 'cancer-curing' diets widely promoted on Indian social media are NOT evidence-based. | 💉 CHEMO [C3-1/C3-2]: Maintain intake during all cycles. Common Indian patient challenge: nausea reducing dal/sabzi intake. Small frequent meals; ginger/ajwain/saunf for nausea. ONS if <75% intake. | 🐟 OMEGA-3 [B5-7]: 2–3 g EPA/day (fish oil or algae-based for vegetarians) — reduces chemo toxicity, preserves lean mass, protective against neuropathy. | ❌ [C3-3]: No glutamine. No high-dose antioxidants during chemotherapy. | 💊 AROMATASE INHIBITOR: PRIORITY in Indian women: Vit D deficiency endemic + AI worsens bone loss → dual risk. Calcium from ragi/sesame/dairy + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise. DEXA annually. AI-arthralgia: omega-3 + haldi (turmeric) anti-inflammatory. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Smooth ragi/oats porridge (full-fat milk + 2 tbsp milk powder + ground flaxseed 1 tsp) + pureed banana + 250 ml ONS — all soft/blended; cool to room temp; avoid acidic/spicy || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Plain khakhra/dry toast + saunf-adrak tea; coconut water sips; room-temp bland foods only; avoid sweet/fatty foods || 🍽 Lunch: 2 ragi roti + palak paneer (80g paneer, minimal oil) + cucumber raita + salad | Ragi + paneer = calcium powerhouse for AI patients || 🕓 Snack: Smooth shrikhand (strained curd + minimal sugar) / banana smoothie (dahi + banana) / coconut milk pudding; AVOID: imli/lemon/spice/rough foods; baking soda + salt gurgle before eating || 🌙 Dinner: 2 whole wheat chapati + moong dal (yellow, easy digest) + stir-fried palak/methi + dahi + salad | Light dinner for better sleep || 🌛 Bedtime: Warm milk + 2 dates (natural melatonin) + 5 walnuts | Sleep + omega-3 || ✅ TASTE CHANGES: Adrak (ginger) and nimbu (lemon) enhance flavour; use hari chutney (mint-coriander); room-temp/cold foods better; metallic taste — use steel/plastic cutlery not aluminium; marinate protein in dahi+haldi. || ✅ WEIGHT GAIN (Chemo/Hormone Therapy): Common in Indian BC patients on Tamoxifen/AI. Reduce maida, sugar, fried foods. Increase millets, vegetables, protein. 30 min brisk walk daily minimum. No crash diets during treatment. BMI target 18.5–22.9 post-treatment. || 🥦 ANTI-CANCER INDIAN FOODS: Haldi (turmeric/curcumin), adrak (ginger), lehsun (garlic), pyaaz (onion — quercetin), amla (Vit C + antioxidants), drumstick leaves (moringa — calcium + iron), methi seeds (blood sugar), tulsi (adaptogen), green tea (EGCG). || Regional: Emphasise whole wheat chapati, bajra/jowar roti, dal, seasonal sabzi; reduce heavy ghee, cream, paneer excess; increase green leafy vegetables. || 💰 Upper-Middle SES: Can include quinoa, Greek yoghurt, salmon, organic produce. Focus on quality over quantity. Avoid over-supplementation. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class II, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 💊 AI PATIENT — CALCIUM FOODS: Ragi (nachni) roti daily, til (sesame) chutney, rajma, dahi, paneer (in moderation), moringa leaves (sahjan), amaranth (rajgira). Sunlight exposure 15–20 min before 10am for Vit D. Annual DEXA scan. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI <18.5 — Energy & protein repletion required. High nutritional risk.
Waist_Risk_Indian: Normal (<75 cm)
Bone_Density_Concern: HIGH — AI-related bone loss. DEXA annually. Calcium 600–1200 mg/day + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Fatigue; Lymphedema; Peripheral Neuropathy; Taste Changes/Chemosensory Alteration
Vitamin_D_IU_per_day: 400 IU/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) — sunlight 15–20 min/day also essential
Calcium_mg_per_day: 600 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) — dietary calcium from dairy/ragi/sesame preferred
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: Dietary omega-3: mustard oil cooking + flaxseed + walnuts + fatty fish (if non-veg) 2x/week
Protein_Source_Note: Vegetarian protein: dal+rice combo (complete AA), paneer, curd, soya, moong, rajma, chickpeas, tofu, amaranth
Soy_Food_Guidance: Whole soy foods (tofu/soya/edamame): 1–2 servings/day SAFE for ER+ Indian BC survivors [evidence reassuring]
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) + Vitamin D 400 IU/day + 15–20 min daily sunlight; Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; LYMPHEDEMA: Progressive resistance IS SAFE — use compression garment; start with light weights, increase gradually; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [South India (Tamil Nadu/Karnataka/Kerala/Andhra)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class I]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 🔴 TNBC [Indian]: High incidence in young premenopausal Indian women. Aggressive chemo → highest nutritional risk. Protein priority 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day. Anti-inflammatory diet. Immunotherapy GI AE management. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].

Adequate protein for tissue health. Avoid very salty foods (sodium). Compression garment during exercise. Progressive resistance exercise IS SAFE. || ⚖ WEIGHT NOTE (Indian BMI): Indian women are at higher metabolic risk at BMI ≥23. Obesity (BMI ≥25) significantly increases BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Post-treatment: maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 [ICMR/WHO Asian cut-offs]. || Regional: Prefer brown/red rice, ragi, sambhar, rasam (anti-inflammatory spices), coconut in moderation; reduce coconut oil excess; increase fibre from drumstick, raw banana. || 💰 Low SES: Focus on cost-effective anti-cancer foods — seasonal vegetables, local millets, dals, eggs, sprouts. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 🔴 TNBC (Indian): Higher prevalence in young Indian women (<40 yrs). Highest metabolic demand. Protein 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day mandatory during chemo. Anti-inflammatory diet: haldi, adrak, omega-3, berries, green tea. Immunotherapy patients: watch for immune-related colitis — low-residue if GI symptoms. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Omega-3 / EPA 2–3 g/day (algae-based DHA if vegetarian) [ESPEN B5-7] — lean mass + neuropathy protection; Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (split: 600mg x2; food sources: ragi, dahi, sesame preferred) + Vitamin D 800–1000 IU/day (AI-related bone loss); Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Megestrol Acetate / short-term Corticosteroid — physician-prescribed [ESPEN B5-1/B5-2] (note DVT risk with megestrol in Indian patients); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Gentle daily walk (10–20 min) / seated yoga; comfort prioritised [ESPEN B4-1]
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [North India (UP/Delhi/Punjab/Haryana)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 🔄 SUBSTRATE [B2-3]: Insulin resistance (common in obese Indian BC patients) → ↑ fat, ↓ refined carbohydrate, prioritise low-GI foods (millets, whole grains, legumes). | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 💉 CHEMO [C3-1/C3-2]: Maintain intake during all cycles. Common Indian patient challenge: nausea reducing dal/sabzi intake. Small frequent meals; ginger/ajwain/saunf for nausea. ONS if <75% intake. | 🐟 OMEGA-3 [B5-7]: 2–3 g EPA/day (fish oil or algae-based for vegetarians) — reduces chemo toxicity, preserves lean mass, protective against neuropathy. | ❌ [C3-3]: No glutamine. No high-dose antioxidants during chemotherapy. | 💊 AROMATASE INHIBITOR: PRIORITY in Indian women: Vit D deficiency endemic + AI worsens bone loss → dual risk. Calcium from ragi/sesame/dairy + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise. DEXA annually. AI-arthralgia: omega-3 + haldi (turmeric) anti-inflammatory. | 🕊 PALLIATIVE [C6-1–C6-3]: Comfort-based Indian foods. No restrictive rules. Family/caregiver involvement in food decisions important in Indian cultural context. Home-cooked preferred. Spiritual/cultural food preferences respected. | 💊 APPETITE [B5-1/B5-2]: Short-term corticosteroids or megestrol acetate (physician-prescribed). Note: megestrol — DVT risk; monitor in Indian patients with higher thrombosis predisposition. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Small portions of favourite Indian comfort foods; warm dalia/khichdi/idli if tolerated; 1 cup chai (weak) or herbal tea || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Favourite sips — coconut water, thin chaas, nimbu pani; small fruit if appetite permits || 🍽 Lunch: Soft khichdi or curd-rice or favourite dal-rice; small portions; texture modified if needed; home-cooked preferred || 🕓 Snack: Whatever is desired; cold foods often preferred; custard/dahi/fruit as tolerated || 🌙 Dinner: Light khichdi or vegetable soup + soft roti/bread; warm haldi doodh if tolerated || 🌛 Bedtime: Warm water/milk as desired; comfort-based only || 🕊 PALLIATIVE [ESPEN C6-3]: No restrictive dietary rules. Comfort and dignity are the goals. Small amounts of favourite foods provide emotional comfort. PN unlikely to benefit unless prognosis >2 months. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class II, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || ✅ UNDERWEIGHT: Fortify ALL Indian meals: add ghee/coconut oil (1 tsp extra), milk powder (2 tbsp) to dalia/oats, peanut chutney, til laddoo, dry fruits. Commercial ONS 2x/day. Target +0.5 kg/week. Khova/mawa laddoo or high-calorie kheer if well tolerated. || 💊 AI PATIENT — CALCIUM FOODS: Ragi (nachni) roti daily, til (sesame) chutney, rajma, dahi, paneer (in moderation), moringa leaves (sahjan), amaranth (rajgira). Sunlight exposure 15–20 min before 10am for Vit D. Annual DEXA scan. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA) + Vitamin D 400 IU/day + 15–20 min daily sunlight; Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; BONE/JOINT PAIN: Low-impact only (swimming, yoga, walking); NO high-impact/contact; physio referral; warm mustard oil massage for joints; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [North India (UP/Delhi/Punjab/Haryana)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 🔄 SUBSTRATE [B2-3]: Insulin resistance (common in obese Indian BC patients) → ↑ fat, ↓ refined carbohydrate, prioritise low-GI foods (millets, whole grains, legumes). | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Plain dry toast/khakhra (2) + adrak-tulsi tea (cold/room temp, anti-nausea); small bites; avoid strong cooking smells; saunf (fennel) water sips || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Plain khakhra/dry toast + saunf-adrak tea; coconut water sips; room-temp bland foods only; avoid sweet/fatty foods || 🍽 Lunch: Soft dal-rice (1 cup each) + 1 tsp ghee (for calories) + steamed vegetable + full-fat dahi + 1 tbsp til/sesame for calcium || 🕓 Snack: 250ml commercial ONS (Pentasure/Ensure HP) + energy-dense snack: paneer cubes (30g) / til-jaggery laddoo (1) / peanut chukli (2) || 🌙 Dinner: Moong dal khichdi (1.5 cups, soft, with ghee 1 tsp) + boiled/steamed fish / paneer curry (soft) + cooked lauki/tinda + warm haldi doodh || 🌛 Bedtime: Full-fat milk (250ml warm) + 1–2 tbsp almond/peanut butter + pinch turmeric OR 250ml ONS supplement || ✅ WEIGHT GAIN (Chemo/Hormone Therapy): Common in Indian BC patients on Tamoxifen/AI. Reduce maida, sugar, fried foods. Increase millets, vegetables, protein. 30 min brisk walk daily minimum. No crash diets during treatment. BMI target 18.5–22.9 post-treatment. || ✅ BONE HEALTH (Metastasis/AI): Calcium-rich Indian foods: ragi (344mg/100g), til (sesame, 975mg/100g), rajma, dahi, paneer, moringa/drumstick leaves (440mg/100g). Vit D from sunlight (15–20 min, before 10am) + supplement. Low-impact exercise only for bone mets. || 🧂 LIMIT (Indian context): Excess ghee/vanaspati/refined oil, maida (refined flour) products (biscuits/namkeen/puri), packaged/processed foods, high-sodium pickles/papad in excess, mithai (sweets), sugar-sweetened drinks (nimbu pani with sugar, lassi with sugar), red/processed meat. || Regional: Emphasise whole wheat chapati, bajra/jowar roti, dal, seasonal sabzi; reduce heavy ghee, cream, paneer excess; increase green leafy vegetables. || 💰 Middle SES: Balanced home-cooking. Weekly fish/egg 2–3x. Millet rotation. Seasonal produce. Avoid processed/packaged foods marketed as 'healthy'. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class II, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI <18.5 — Energy & protein repletion required. High nutritional risk.
Waist_Risk_Indian: Central Obesity (≥80 cm — Indian Women Threshold)
Bone_Density_Concern: HIGH — AI-related bone loss. DEXA annually. Calcium 600–1200 mg/day + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Alopecia; Peripheral Neuropathy; Taste Changes/Chemosensory Alteration; Weight Gain
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: 2–3 g EPA/DHA/day — fish oil supplement [ESPEN B5-7]
Protein_Source_Note: Protein: eggs (2/day) + dal + paneer + curd + legumes + soya
Soy_Food_Guidance: Whole soy foods (tofu/soya/edamame): 1–2 servings/day SAFE for ER+ Indian BC survivors [evidence reassuring]
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]

NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.

Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. ONS if <75% intake. | 🐟 OMEGA-3 [B5-7]: 2–3 g EPA/day (fish oil or algae-based for vegetarians) — reduces chemo toxicity, preserves lean mass, protective against neuropathy. | ❌ [C3-3]: No glutamine. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

PN unlikely to benefit unless prognosis >2 months. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class I, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600–1000 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) + Vitamin D 400–800 IU/day — endemic Vit D deficiency in India; Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); ELDERLY: Chair-based resistance, balance exercises (Vrikshasana/tree pose), fall prevention; supervised sessions at physiotherapy/yoga centre; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [East India (West Bengal/Odisha/Bihar/Jharkhand)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class I]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Monitor PO4, K+, Mg2+. Vitamin B1 200–300 mg/day. | 🔴 TNBC [Indian]: High incidence in young premenopausal Indian women. Aggressive chemo → highest nutritional risk. Protein priority 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day. Anti-inflammatory diet. Immunotherapy GI AE management. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Fortified dalia/oats porridge (full-fat milk + 1 egg whisked in / extra milk powder 3 tbsp) + banana + 1 tbsp peanut butter + 250 ml ONS (Ensure/Pentasure/Fresubin) + green tea || 🕙 Mid-Morning: High-calorie Indian shake — full-fat milk + banana + 2 tbsp peanut butter/almond butter + 1 tbsp ground flaxseed + 1 tsp jaggery (~450 kcal) + ONS if appetite poor || 🍽 Lunch: Soft dal-rice (1 cup each) + 1 tsp ghee (for calories) + steamed vegetable + full-fat dahi + 1 tbsp til/sesame for calcium || 🕓 Snack: 250ml commercial ONS (Pentasure/Ensure HP) + energy-dense snack: paneer cubes (30g) / til-jaggery laddoo (1) / peanut chukli (2) || 🌙 Dinner: Moong dal khichdi (1.5 cups, soft, with ghee 1 tsp) + boiled/steamed fish / paneer curry (soft) + cooked lauki/tinda + warm haldi doodh || 🌛 Bedtime: Full-fat milk (250ml warm) + 1–2 tbsp almond/peanut butter + pinch turmeric OR 250ml ONS supplement || 🍷 ALCOHOL: ZERO — complete avoidance mandatory [ESPEN C5-2]. Weekly fish/egg 2–3x. Millet rotation. Seasonal produce. Avoid processed/packaged foods marketed as 'healthy'. || ⚠ OBESITY (Obese Class I, Indian cut-off ≥25): Obesity significantly increases BC recurrence risk in Indian women. Post-treatment gradual weight loss (0.5 kg/week max). No energy restriction during active treatment. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet: dal-sabzi-millet base + minimal ghee/oil. Walk 45 min/day. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 🔴 TNBC (Indian): Higher prevalence in young Indian women (<40 yrs). Highest metabolic demand. Protein 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day mandatory during chemo. Anti-inflammatory diet: haldi, adrak, omega-3, berries, green tea. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.

Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 1000–1200 mg/day (split: 600mg x2; food sources: ragi, dahi, sesame preferred) + Vitamin D 800–1000 IU/day (AI-related bone loss); Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Megestrol Acetate / short-term Corticosteroid — physician-prescribed [ESPEN B5-1/B5-2] (note DVT risk with megestrol in Indian patients); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; SARCOPENIA: Priority resistance training + leucine-rich protein (dal + paneer + dahi combination, 2–3g leucine/meal); AI PATIENTS: Weight-bearing exercise ESSENTIAL for bone health (walking/stair climbing 30 min/day minimum); reduces AI-related arthralgia; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [West India (Maharashtra/Gujarat/Rajasthan)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OBESITY [Obese Class II]: Indian BMI ≥25 = Obese. Metabolic syndrome highly prevalent. Obesity is independent risk factor for BC recurrence and mortality in Indian women. Weight management essential post-treatment. | 🥗 NUTRITION [B3-1]: Active nutritional counselling + ONS if enriched Indian diet insufficient. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No energy restriction during treatment. No unproven diets — ketogenic, prolonged fasting, 'cancer-curing' diets widely promoted on Indian social media are NOT evidence-based. | 💊 AROMATASE INHIBITOR: PRIORITY in Indian women: Vit D deficiency endemic + AI worsens bone loss → dual risk. Calcium from ragi/sesame/dairy + Vit D 800–1000 IU/day + weight-bearing exercise. DEXA annually. AI-arthralgia: omega-3 + haldi (turmeric) anti-inflammatory. | 💊 APPETITE [B5-1/B5-2]: Short-term corticosteroids or megestrol acetate (physician-prescribed). Note: megestrol — DVT risk; monitor in Indian patients with higher thrombosis predisposition. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | 💪 SARCOPENIA (Indian): Low grip strength — sarcopenia prevalent in Indian BC patients even at normal/overweight BMI (sarcopenic obesity). Leucine-rich protein + resistance training essential. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].

ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [East India (West Bengal/Odisha/Bihar/Jharkhand)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 🔄 SUBSTRATE [B2-3]: Insulin resistance (common in obese Indian BC patients) → ↑ fat, ↓ refined carbohydrate, prioritise low-GI foods (millets, whole grains, legumes). | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | ⚠ INDIAN OVERWEIGHT (BMI 23–24.9): Indian overweight threshold — metabolic risk begins. Lifestyle modification: Mediterranean-Indian diet pattern + 45 min walk daily. | 🚨 NUTRITION [B3-1]: IMMEDIATE intervention. ONS (Pentasure/Ensure/Fresubin); escalate to EN if oral <50% target >1 week. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No unproven restrictive diets. Beware of social media misinformation about 'anti-cancer' diets in Indian context. | 🏥 MEDICAL NUTRITION [B3-3]: EN preferred (nasogastric/PEG); PN if EN not feasible. | ⚠ REFEEDING [B3-4]: Slow reintroduction if prolonged malnutrition. Small frequent meals; ginger/ajwain/saunf for nausea. ONS if <75% intake. | 🐟 OMEGA-3 [B5-7]: 2–3 g EPA/day (fish oil or algae-based for vegetarians) — reduces chemo toxicity, preserves lean mass, protective against neuropathy. | ❌ [C3-3]: No glutamine. No high-dose antioxidants during chemotherapy. | 💊 TAMOXIFEN: AVOID grapefruit/kinnow. ZERO alcohol. Endometrial monitoring. Fibre-rich Indian diet may improve efficacy. Flaxseed safe. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].

Vit D from sunlight (15–20 min, before 10am) + supplement. Low-impact exercise only for bone mets. || 🏃 EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2/C5-1]: 150–300 min/week moderate aerobic (brisk walk, yoga, cycling, swimming) + 2–3x/week resistance. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.
